# ai.STARTUPJURY — prototype parity findings

Generated 2026-09-09 by an 82-agent audit (41 lanes, each adversarially verified) of the eleven role
prototypes and the two written product specs against `main` @ `8822db2`. **1,107 findings** survive
verification; 6 were refuted and removed.

Every finding has a stable id (`F0001`…). Sessions claim ids from `plan_parity.md` and tick them off
there. Machine-readable copy: `docs/PARITY-FINDINGS.json`.

| Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **P0** | a screen, workflow or configuration surface the prototype specifies is entirely absent |
| **P1** | the screen exists but a major element is missing (columns, chart, modal, action, tab) |
| **P2** | a meaningful contained difference (labels, filter, export, layout shape) |
| **P3** | cosmetic |

`verified` = an adversarial reviewer confirmed the claim · `severity adjusted` = the reviewer re-graded it ·
`found on review` = the reviewer added it because the first pass missed it.

> Three findings must **not** be built as drawn — see *Do not build as drawn* in `plan_parity.md`.

### F0038 · `P1` · All three sections are unreachable for 9 of the 11 role prototypes — the repo gates the whole Admin console to admin/superuser
*Admin console (shell) → CRM sync · Notifications · Audit log — role-gating · effort M · found on review*

This is load-bearing for Notifications specifically: the prototype scopes it to 'your account', so a jury member must be able to turn off their own 'New pitchdeck submitted' mail, and today there is no screen they can reach to do it. Two decisions are needed and neither is recorded anywhere in docs/: (a) whether every role really gets a console entry, and (b) whether the non-admin console is read-only — the prototype markup says it is NOT, which is a plausible prototype oversight for CRM credentials and billing but is clearly intentional for Notifications.
- **Prototype** — Every one of the 11 live prototypes ships an Admin console containing these three sections, not just the admin/superuser ones. AISJ_IC_Jury_V4/admin/_scripts.js:2 and AISJ_VC_Analyst_V1/admin/_scripts.js:20 both read `var secs=['fw','wt','rb','qb','tm','crm','bl','pc','nt','al','uc','br']` — the 12-section non-admin console, which still includes crm, nt and al. I ran cmp across all 11: admin/s-crm.html is byte-identical in every prototype including Jury, PA, Analyst and Associate; s-nt.html and s-al.html are identical within each edition and differ across editions only in seeded actor names and 'IC member' vs 'Jury member submitted scores'. The brief's assumption that the non-admin consoles are a read-only variant does NOT hold for these three sections — the jury console carries the same live Connect/Disconnect buttons, the same 10 writable toggles and the same full audit trail. s-nt.html's subtitle scopes it per person: 'Control which platform events trigger email and in-app alerts for your account.'

Only admin (plus the superuser bypass documented in the file header) reaches /app/admin; program_manager, program_associate and jury in the incubator, and partner, ic_member, associate and analyst in the VC, get no Admin console item at all. src/client/routes/AdminConsolePage.tsx has no section routing to gate in the first place.
- **Fix** — Split the console into per-section role lists rather than one nav item: keep tm/crm/bl/pc/su*/uc admin-only, and open nt (per-user, all roles) and al (read-only, all roles) to every internal role. Confirm the read-only question with the client before shipping — flag that giving jury the prototype's live CRM credentials and Credits & billing screens is almost certainly not intended.

### F0040 · `P1` · No per-question Q&A model — questions and founder answers are each a single text blob, so bank questions could never be tracked, answered or reported individually
*Admin console › Evaluation › Question bank (s-qb) → founder clarification round-trip — data-model · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Distinct from the auditor's claim 9 (which is about where question TEXT comes from): even with a bank wired up, there is nowhere to record which bank question was asked on a deck, who asked it, whether the founder answered that specific question, or when — so 'which areas did the founder actually address' can never be computed, and the Query screen's resolution state stays all-or-nothing per letter. The spec chapter that specifies this schema was not cited anywhere in the ten findings.
- **Prototype** — admin/s-qb.html models every question as its own addressable row: 68 `.q-row` elements, each with a `.q-num` ordinal (Q1..Qn) and its own `.q-edit` control, grouped under 13 `.qb-area` accordions with a per-area '<n> questions' count. Both written specs make the round trip per-question: live/specs/incubator.html suggested schema 'founder_clarifications ( id, deck_id ⟶ decks, asked_by ⟶ users, question text, answer text, answered_at )' and cross-cutting behaviour 'Founder clarification portal: founders can respond to evaluator questions (round-trip Q&A tied to a deck)'; live/specs/vc.html carries the identical rows.
- **Repository** — migrations/0001_init.sql:122-131 — queries(id, deck_id, questions TEXT, email_status, founder_response TEXT, created_at, resolved_at): one blob out, one blob back, no asked_by, no per-question answer, no answered_at. src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:495-499 stores the whole letter in `questions`. src/client/routes/FounderPortal.tsx:144-165 renders query.questions as one <p> and offers a single textarea posting respondQuery(query.id, response). Repo-wide grep for founder_clarifications / answered_at returns 0 hits.
- **Fix** — Introduce query_questions(id, query_id, bank_question_id NULL, area_parameter_id, ordinal, question, answer, answered_at) keyed off the existing queries row; render one answer field per question in FounderPortal and roll answered/unanswered up to the Query screen.

### F0041 · `P1` · Clarification questions are never auto-triggered — the entire 'send automatically when the AI detects weak signal' mechanism the question bank exists to feed has no implementation
*Admin console › Evaluation › Question bank (s-qb), cross-checked against Scoring framework (s-fw) — automation · effort L · found on review*

- **Gap** — The prototype's clarification loop is automatic and admin-switchable; the repo's is 100% manual. Even once a question bank exists, nothing would fire it: there is no trigger on evaluation completion, no toggle to turn it off, and no detection of 'contradictory' signal at all (only weak and missing are derived). This is the mechanism that makes the question bank worth building, and the auditor's ten findings cover the bank's data/UI but never state that the trigger itself is absent.
- **Prototype** — admin/s-qb.html sec-sub: 'These questions are auto-triggered to the startup when the AI detects weak, missing, or contradictory signal in a given area.' admin/s-fw.html 'AI engine behaviour' card, second tog-row: 'Auto-trigger clarification questions' / 'Send targeted questions to startup when AI detects weak signal', shipped with class `tog on` (default ON). Byte-identical in all 11 role consoles.
- **Repository** — The only code path that creates a query is the manual pipeline.post('/decks/:id/queries', requireRole(...)) at src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:487-499, which returns 400 questions_required unless a human supplies free text, and is reached only from QueryPage's Send button. `INSERT INTO queries` appears nowhere in src/ except that handler (migrations/0005_seed_founder_decks.sql:11 and 0020_seed_demo_refresh.sql:653 are demo seeds). src/server/ai/evaluate.ts and src/server/queue.ts never touch the queries table after scoring. src/server/scheduled.ts exports only runReminders and runStuckSweep (the two cron jobs wired in src/server/index.ts:71-77). org_settings (migrations/0001_init.sql:18-26; its only later ALTER is criteria_version in 0009) has no automation toggle column, and no config route writes one.
- **Fix** — Add org_settings.auto_query_enabled (default 1) plus the s-fw toggle, and fire query creation from the post-evaluation path in src/server/ai/evaluate.ts / queue.ts when weak or missing areas exist, drawing question text from the new bank; keep the manual Query screen as the override.

### F0042 · `P1` · The 'weak signal' that selects clarification areas is the All-Decks cohort rating threshold, not the rubric's Weak band — moving a cohort threshold silently re-targets founder questions
*Admin console › Evaluation › Rubric anchors (s-rb) ⟷ Question bank trigger (s-qb / s-fw) — correctness · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Two unrelated scales are conflated. scoring.ts:26-40 even documents that the cohort thresholds are 'Distinct from the fixed rubric signal bands above', yet the clarification loop is gated on them: an admin raising 'Poor — below' from 5.0 to 6.5 to re-bucket decks on the All Decks overview also widens which parameters get asked about, and an area scored 5.5 is never queried even though the BRD calls 5–6 Moderate and 3–4 Weak. Fixing the band scale (auditor claim 3) alone does not fix this, because the trigger never reads a band at all.
- **Prototype** — s-qb sec-sub scopes the trigger to 'weak, missing, or contradictory signal in a given area' — an AREA-level judgement, which s-rb and both specs define only on the BRD five-band scale (live/specs/incubator.html §7: v≥3 → Weak(3), else Insufficient(4); admin/_scripts.js:263 RUBRICS gives each area its own 3–4 and 0–2 descriptors). The cohort thresholds are a deliberately separate concept in the same console: admin/s-fw.html's 'Cohort rating thresholds' block says 'Define the rating bands evaluators see on the All Decks overview' (Best / Mediocre / Poor, #thr-best 7.0, #thr-poor 5.0).
- **Repository** — src/server/routes/decks.ts:63-65 derives weak_areas as `... AND s.value < (SELECT o.threshold_mediocre FROM org_settings o WHERE o.edition = d.edition)`. threshold_mediocre is the admin-editable cohort threshold (migrations/0001_init.sql:25; src/shared/scoring.ts:36-40 cohortRating; ConfigPage ThresholdsSection; PUT /api/config/thresholds at src/server/routes/config.ts:312). Those labels flow straight into the founder letter via src/shared/queries.ts:47 and QueryPage.tsx:145. No rubric band value is consulted anywhere in the clarification path.
- **Fix** — Once the 5-band scale lands, derive weak_areas from the rubric band (value < 5, i.e. Weak or Insufficient) or from an explicit configurable clarification threshold, and leave threshold_mediocre to cohort rating only.

### F0059 · `P1` · GET /api/activity cannot back an audit log at all — hard cap of 50, no pagination, no date range, no filters, no export
*Admin console → System → Audit log — api-capability · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Audited item 4 treats this as a placement-and-shape problem ('wrong place and wrong shape'), which implies the fix is to re-render the same endpoint inside the console. It is not: any Audit log section built on /api/activity can never display more than the 50 most recent workspace events, can never be paged back to the '3 Jun' rows the prototype shows, and can never be filtered by category, actor or date or exported. The endpoint needs cursor pagination and a filter surface regardless of how the event model in items 5-9 is fixed, and that work is invisible in the current findings.
- **Prototype** — admin/s-al.html sec-sub: 'Full timestamped trail of all configuration changes, score overrides, team actions, and billing events.' The seeded rows span three days and mix clock times, 'Yesterday' and absolute dates ('3 Jun'), so the section is explicitly a historical trail, not a recent-activity peek.
- **Repository** — src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:795 — `const limit = Math.min(Math.max(Number(c.req.query("limit") ?? 12) || 12, 1), 50);`. The query at pipeline.ts:817-824 is `ORDER BY e.created_at DESC, e.rowid DESC LIMIT ?` with no OFFSET, no cursor and no date predicate; the only filters are programId and cohortId. The response (pipeline.ts:840-853) returns a bare `events` array with no total and no next cursor. The deck-scoped alternative, GET /decks/:id/events (pipeline.ts:742), is unbounded but per-deck, and its client helper src/client/api.ts:458 getDeckEvents has zero call sites.
- **Fix** — Add cursor pagination (created_at + rowid keyset, `next_cursor` in the response), a `from`/`to` date range, and actor/category/action filters to GET /api/activity; keep the 12-row Dashboard rail as a `limit=12` caller so nothing regresses. Add CSV export once categories exist. Size this alongside the schema work in item 5 — the new event table should be designed with the keyset index from the start.

### F0060 · `P1` · Notification preferences are per-USER with a specified default mask — the repo has no per-user settings storage of any kind, so claim 2's org-level framing would build the wrong model
*Admin console → System → Notifications — data-model · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Claim 2 reports this as an admin/org-level surface ('An admin cannot see or change which events email them'), which would lead to a single org_settings JSON column. The prototype requires a row per (user × event) with a seeded 8-on/2-off default applied to every user at creation (src/server/routes/users.ts) and to all 30-odd seeded demo logins, plus a suppression check inside sendEmail so the 7 existing call sites stay unchanged. That is a materially different and larger build than the reported gap describes, and getting it wrong is expensive to unwind once demo data is seeded.
- **Prototype** — admin/s-nt.html subtitle: '…trigger email and in-app alerts for your account' — per person, not per workspace, and the section ships in all 11 role consoles (see the previous item). The seed also fixes the DEFAULT MASK: 8 of the 10 `.tog` elements carry class `on` and exactly 2 do not — 'Startup responded to clarification questions' and 'New team member accepted invite' — and the VC copy (AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/admin/s-nt.html) uses the identical 8-on/2-off split, so the defaults are deliberate, not incidental.
- **Repository** — There is no per-user preference storage anywhere. `users` (migrations/0001_init.sql:5-14, plus every ALTER — 0015_roles_users.sql:19 user_type, 0021_alias_titles_and_tags.sql:10 title) has no preferences column and no side table. The only settings table is `org_settings` (migrations/0001_init.sql:18), a per-EDITION singleton keyed on `edition` — one row for the whole workspace, which cannot express a per-person mask. src/client/routes/AccountPage.tsx has profile fields and the alias title only, with no settings section to hang toggles on. src/server/email/outbox.ts sendEmail has no recipient-preference lookup and no suppression seam.
- **Fix** — Add `notification_prefs (user_id, event_key, enabled)` with the 10 event keys, seed the 8-on/2-off default in a migration for existing users and in the create-user path for new ones, expose GET/PUT /api/notifications/prefs, and put the lookup inside sendEmail keyed on toEmail so no call site changes. Note that only 1 of the 10 events has a producer today (audited item 3), so the toggles ship inert for 9 until those producers exist — sequence this after the producers or the section is a dead screen.

### F0061 · `P1` · Roster has no re-role, no rename and no member removal — the API supports two of the three and nothing calls it
*Admin console → Team & roles — missing-action · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — An admin who mis-assigns a role at creation, or whose staff member changes job, cannot fix it from the console — the only escape is a hand-crafted PATCH. Removing a departed member is absent end-to-end (no API, no UI); deactivation is the only approximation, and it leaves the row and the seat in place. The auditor's claims 7/8/9 cover the pending badge, the permissions matrix and the workspace toggle, but never the roster's own Edit/Remove actions.
- **Prototype** — live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/admin/s-tm.html — the members card header carries an 'Invite member' button, and admin/_scripts.js:119-136 tmRender() ends every row with `.t-acts`: `<button class="t-btn">Edit</button><button class="t-btn del">Remove</button>` for active members and `Resend` / `Cancel` for the pending one (:126-127). 'Delete user' is also one of the grantable tasks in the permissions matrix (admin/_scripts.js:176 `{id:'deleteuser', l:'Delete user'}`), alongside 'Activate user' and 'Deactivate user'. Byte-identical in AISJ_ICAdmin_V6 and both VC admin builds.
- **Repository** — src/client/routes/AdminConsolePage.tsx:213-228 renders exactly one row action — Activate/Deactivate — and the only other per-row control is the alias-title input at :170-198. Meanwhile src/server/routes/users.ts:302-348 (PATCH /api/users/:id) already validates and applies `role` (:320-325) and `name` (:317-318), and src/client/api.ts:791-800 exposes both in updateUser(), so the re-role/rename API is live but has no caller. There is no DELETE route for users anywhere: users.ts registers only GET "/" (:173), PATCH "/me" (:196), POST "/" (:222) and PATCH "/:id" (:302), and `grep -rn '\.delete(' src/server/routes/*.ts` finds delete routes only in config.ts and programs.ts.
- **Fix** — Add a role <select> and a Remove control to each manageable row in AdminConsolePage (reusing updateUser for role/name), and add a guarded DELETE /api/users/:id (block self, block superuser, same-edition only) or an explicit soft-delete, mirroring the prototype's Edit / Remove pair.

### F0062 · `P1` · No way to nominate or change the account's Super User — ownership is permanently whatever the seed created
*Admin console → Team & roles (cross-ref: Setup overlay → Add team members) — user-management · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Account ownership can never be transferred, nominated or recovered. If the seeded superuser leaves the org, the account has no owner and no path to appoint one — the prototype treats nominating exactly one super user as a required, changeable step.

The flow itself is _rest.html:1206 `#su-superbox` on the sus-team screen, rendered by _scripts.js:3247-3260 `renderSuper()` in three states — 'You are the super user', 'Super user — {email} · only one super user per account' with a `su-chgbtn` 'Change', and a required nomination form ('Nominate a super user' + email + plan select + 'Set super user', note 'A super user has full platform access… Only one super user is allowed per account'). Handlers `suSetSuper()` :3262-3266 and `suClearSuper()` :3268. tmRoles.inc/inv both list 'Super user' / 'Managing Partner/Super user' as a real role.

### F0063 · `P1` · Spec §10 grants Program Managers and Client Admins parameter configuration by default; the repo hard-codes it to admin/superuser with no grant path
*Admin console → Team & roles (permission defaults) / Core Parameters — role-gating · effort M · found on review*

The role sidebars agree: si-coreparams is present in AISJ_IC_PM_V5/_sidebar.html:10, AISJ_IC_PA_V3, AISJ_VC_Partner_V1, AISJ_VC_Associate_V1, AISJ_VC_Analyst_V1 and AISJ_VC_IC_member_V2 (absent only in the IC Jury build).
- **Repository** — src/shared/nav.ts:105 (incubator) and :173 (VC) both declare `{ id: "coreparams", … roles: ["admin"] }`, so a PM/PA/partner/associate/analyst never sees the screen and RequireNav blocks the route. src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:32 `const canEdit = user?.role === "admin" || user?.role === "superuser";`. Server-side, src/server/routes/config.ts:151, 215, 261 and 291 all use requireRole("admin"), and src/server/auth/middleware.ts:25 bypasses only `superuser` — program_manager is refused 403.
- **Fix** — Give `coreparams` roles ["admin","program_manager"] (and the VC equivalents the spec implies), let MyParamsPage/ConfigPage compute canEdit from that same source, and relax the server guards to requireRole("admin","program_manager") — ideally reading a persisted permission row once the matrix from claim 8 exists, so the default is data rather than another constant.

### F0081 · `P1` · A role/additional parameter can never be given a weight — both specs require raising it to 5% or 10%
*Area weights (s-wt) — Additional configurable parameters — missing-capability · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — The spec's stated escalation path — an org promotes one of its 9 role parameters into the weighted composite at 5% or 10% — is not representable. The 0-weight informational status is hard-coded at INSERT and defended by an explicit 400 on the one route that could change it, so this needs a schema-adjacent change plus a UI, not a config edit. (Note the build's counter-invariant, FINISH-PLAN.md:62/184/383, 'composite stays core-13 = 100%', is a deliberate design stance — but it was never reconciled against this spec clause, and no doc mentions the 5%/10% option at all.)
- **Prototype** — Both written specs say it three times each, independently of the prototype markup. incubator §6.2 / vc §6.2: 'Default weight Informational (not weighted into the composite **unless the org (fund) raises it to 5% / 10%**).' §7 Scoring & Aggregation: 'Role-custom parameters default to Informational and are excluded from the composite **unless weighted (5% / 10%)**.' And the suggested schema in §9 types the column as `weight[ Informational | 5% | 10% | numeric for standard ]`.
- **Repository** — No path exists to set it. src/server/routes/config.ts:246 inserts every additional param with the weight literal baked into the SQL: `INSERT INTO parameters (…, weight, informational, …) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 0, 1, ?, ?, ?, 1)`. The only weight editor, PUT /api/config/parameters, actively refuses informational rows — config.ts:170 `if (!p || p.informational === 1) return c.json({ error: "invalid_param" }, 400)`. PUT /api/config/additional-params/:id (config.ts:258-286) accepts only `name` and `prompt`. MyParamsPage.tsx renders no weight field. So the value is unreachable from the UI, the API and the admin surface alike.
- **Fix** — Allow PUT /api/config/parameters (or a dedicated route) to set weight ∈ {0, 5, 10} on informational params, surface it as a select on MyParamsPage next to the name/prompt editors, and decide explicitly whether a promoted param joins the core-13 denominator or forms a documented 100+N total.

### F0082 · `P1` · The nine seeded role parameters do not match the specs' canonical tables in either edition
*Area weights (s-wt) — Additional configurable parameters — spec-divergence · effort M · found on review*

Since these are the exact parameters each role scores and the AI pre-fills from their prompts (spec §10: 'the 3 role parameters configured in My Parameters are the exact parameters that role scores'), the build evaluates every deck against a different rubric than the specification defines — and 'TRL stage' in particular (a named deliverable in the incubator PM lens) is scored nowhere.
- **Prototype** — Both specs give a canonical 3×3 table and the incubator one adds a rule making it binding: 'Consistency rule: **these role-parameter names are canonical across every file.** The Super User / Admin "My Parameters — Role configuration" panel defines them for all roles.' Incubator §6.2 — Program Manager: TRL stage · Product-Market Fit · Traction; Program Associate: Program fit · Investment stage · Ask; Jury Member: Barriers of entry · Scalability · Industry growth. VC §6.2 (JP_ADDL) — Investment Associate: Thesis fit · Investment stage · Ask / Ticket size fit; Partner/Principal: TRL stage · Product-Market Fit · Traction; IC Member: Barriers of entry · Scalability · Exit attractiveness. Each row also carries a specific scorer-facing description and AI extraction prompt.
- **Repository** — migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql seeds entirely different names and prompts: incubator PA = 'Program & Mandate Fit' / 'Application Readiness' / 'Founder Coachability Signal'; PM = 'Program Fit' / 'Mentor Engagement Potential' / 'Cohort Contribution Potential'; jury = 'Founder Resilience & Coachability' / 'Product-Market Fit Signal' / 'Team Execution Capability'. VC associate = 'Thesis & Mandate Fit' / 'Deal Readiness' / 'Founder Conviction Signal'; partner = 'Ownership & Return Math' / 'Portfolio Construction Fit' / 'Conviction to Sponsor'; ic_member = 'Founder Resilience & Coachability' / 'Product-Market Fit Signal' / 'Team Execution Capability'. Not one of the 18 spec names appears in the repo: grep -rn 'TRL|Barriers of entry|Exit attractiveness|Thesis fit|Investment stage' over src/, migrations/, docs/FINISH-PLAN.md and HANDOFF.md returns zero hits, so no decision to diverge was ever recorded.
- **Fix** — Reconcile the two lists explicitly: either reseed migrations/0013 with the specs' canonical names/descriptions/prompts, or record a decision in FINISH-PLAN §8 that the seeded set supersedes the spec table and why.

### F0088 · `P1` · No Organization / Fund entity — every billing object the spec anchors on org_id has nothing to hang from; plan and credits are per-EDITION globals
*Credits & billing (s-bl) — spec §5/§13 — data-model · effort L · found on review*

- **Gap** — Claims 2, 6, 7 and 10 each report a missing billing object (ledger, enterprise tier, org plans, subscriptions) without naming the reason none of them can be built as specified: there is no customer record to attach them to. Credits and plan are shared by every user of an edition, so two customers cannot hold different balances, and 'per-org' anything — subscription, seat allowance, invoice, trial grant — has no key. This is the structural precondition for the whole lane and it is unreported; whoever picks up the billing work needs it stated before they start, together with the decision on whether single-tenant stays.
- **Prototype** — spec-incubator.html.txt:11 lists Organization as a core entity and :136 draws "Organization 1---1 Subscription ---(plan tier) 1---inf CreditLedgerEntry"; §13 anchors all three billing tables on it — subscriptions(… org_id ⟶ organizations …):234, credit_ledger(… org_id ⟶ organizations …):235, support_tickets(… org_id ⟶ organizations …):236 (vc-spec.txt:219-221 uses fund_id ⟶ funds). §14 exposes it as GET /orgs/:id/credits. The prototype sells to organizations throughout: ORG_PLANS 25-seat / 100-seat enterprise SKUs, AET_PLANS seat caps, s-bl's "Enterprise · 5 seats".
- **Repository** — No organizations/funds table exists — `grep -c "CREATE TABLE" migrations/*.sql` totals 26 and none is an org. Billing state lives in org_settings, keyed by edition: migrations/0001_init.sql:18-26 (edition PRIMARY KEY, plan, credits_balance), with the file's own header at :1 reading "Single-tenant: one implicit organization". Every credit path is edition-scoped: reserveCredits/refundCredits in src/server/decks/versions.ts:40-55, and config.ts:377/400 "UPDATE org_settings … WHERE edition = ?". HANDOFF.md:621 records the single-tenant choice as deliberate.
- **Fix** — Decide explicitly whether the product stays single-tenant. If billing is to be built, introduce organizations/funds and re-key org_settings, credit_ledger, subscriptions and tickets onto it; if not, record that the billing SKUs are demo-only and cannot be per-customer.

### F0112 · `P1` · The sign-up sub-status enum (initiated → progress → completed → onboarded) does not exist — the repo models the whole sign-up as one hop

Without intermediate states a deck cannot be 'completed but seatless' (the exact predicate claim 9's badge is defined on), the four workspace stage chips have nothing to drive them, and 'documents submitted, awaiting countersign' is indistinguishable from 'invite just sent'. This should be sequenced before the seat and workspace work rather than discovered during it.
- **Prototype** — specs/incubator.html §Key enums: 'Sign-up / pipeline status: shortlisted, rejected, initiated, progress, completed, onboarded, archived'; §8.2: 'initiated → progress → completed → onboarded is the sign-up happy path'. The prototype's four workspace stages are computed directly from these values — AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:2013-2020 suSignupBody maps sg==='initiated' → Founder response active, sg==='progress' → Verify & countersign active, after(['completed','onboarded','archived']) → Completed done — and the seatless card at :2050-2055 renders only once sg is 'completed', with suAllocSeat (:2069) advancing it to 'onboarded'.
- **Repository** — src/pipeline/incubator.ts:24-25 defines exactly two sign-up statuses, `signup` and `onboard_ready` (terminal), and :123/:130 exactly two actions, `send_signup` and `complete_signup`. src/client/routes/StagePage.tsx:352-353 renders the 'Sign-up status' column as a bare `deck.status` string — there is no initiated / progress / completed value anywhere in src/ or migrations/. No sign-up token table either (`grep -rniE "signup.?token|signup.?link|/signup/" src/ migrations/` returns nothing), so the prototype's emailed https://startupjury.in/signup/<token> link has no counterpart, though resubmit_tokens (migrations/0017) is the working pattern.
- **Fix** — Extend the incubator pipeline with initiated / progress / completed between `signup` and `onboard_ready` (or hold them on a `signups.status` column so the deck status stays coarse), drive the workspace stage chips and the seatless predicate from it, and mint a tokenized founder sign-up link modelled on resubmit_tokens.

### F0167 · `P2` · Per-area scoring is whole-number only; the spec mandates 0.5 steps
*Scoring framework (s-fw) — Score composition / score scale — spec-divergence · effort S · found on review*

- **Gap** — An evaluator cannot express a 7.5. Since the spec's five-band mapping puts boundaries at whole numbers (v≥9, v≥7, v≥5, v≥3), half-steps are the only way to score within a band, and the claim-3 'Score scale' control would be meaningless without the underlying granularity.
- **Prototype** — incubator/vc spec §7 Scoring & Aggregation, first line: 'Per-area score: **integer/half-step 0–10 (step 0.5)**. AI supplies a suggested value; the human can override.' This is the spec-side counterpart of the s-fw 'Score scale' control the auditor reported as missing (claim 3), but it is a behavioural requirement rather than a settings one.
- **Repository** — src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx:245-248 `<input type="range" min={0} max={10} step={1}>` for core parameters, and :303-306 the identical control for additional parameters — the only two score inputs in the app. Nothing else in src/client/components/*.tsx sets a step. The storage layer is fine (migrations/0001_init.sql:91 `value REAL`) and the server clamps but does not round (pipeline.ts:371 `Math.max(0, Math.min(10, …))`), so this is purely the input granularity.
- **Fix** — Set step={0.5} on both range inputs and format the displayed value to one decimal; no schema or server change is needed.

### F0211 · `P1` · Already-assigned decks are listed and selectable in panel 1, but confirming them fails server-side — there is no assigned→assigned re-assign transition, and the confirm loop half-writes before erroring
*panel-assign (col 1 + confirm) — functionality · incubator · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Selecting any deck that already shows an assignee and pressing Confirm returns 409 unknown_action. Worse, because confirm() writes sequentially, a mixed selection (some ai_evaluated, some assigned) commits the earlier decks, then aborts on the first assigned one — leaving a partial assignment on the server while the UI shows only a generic failure and no indication of which decks were written. The user is offered an action the pipeline cannot perform.
- **Prototype** — panels/Incubator_Final_files_AISJ_IC_SuserV11_HTM/_scripts.js:840-848 (`TaxPilot` seeds with `assigned:true`), :937-939 renderAsDecks gives an assigned deck `rowCls = 'as-deck-row ... assigned'` but keeps `onclick="asToggleDeck(i)"` and an enabled checkbox, and :1132 asConfirm re-marks it assigned — i.e. the prototype explicitly supports adding evaluators to a deck that is already assigned (which is the whole point of its deck×member cross product).
- **Repository** — src/client/routes/AssignPage.tsx:47-50 — `rows` keeps `d.statusId === "ai_evaluated" || d.statusId === "assigned"`, and :211-213 badges the existing assignee, so an assigned deck is offered for selection. But src/pipeline/incubator.ts:73-79 defines `assign_jury` ONLY as `from: "ai_evaluated" → to: "assigned"`; there is no transition out of `assigned` other than `start_jury_eval`. src/pipeline/index.ts:78-79 returns `{ok:false, error:"unknown_action"}` when no transition matches, and src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:289-293 maps that to HTTP 409. src/client/routes/AssignPage.tsx:104-118 awaits `assignDeck` once per allocation row with no rollback and a single `catch` that sets the generic string 'Assignment failed. Try again.'
- **Fix** — Either add an `assigned → assigned` re-assign transition (with its own action + event) and surface a 'Re-assign' confirmation, or exclude already-assigned decks from panel 1 selection (show them read-only). Also report per-deck success/failure from confirm() instead of a single generic error.

### F0215 · `P1` · Selecting several founders mails every one of them the union of ALL selected startups' flagged areas, directly contradicting the screen's own confidentiality promise

The repo introduced the per-area body that the prototype does not have, then broadcast it — this is a confidentiality defect the prototype cannot exhibit, and it is exactly the bulk-select path the prototype's `.q-bulk` bar (panel-query.html:240-246) is built to encourage.

### F0216 · `P1` · The composed Subject is discarded and the body is re-wrapped by the server, so what staff see in the compose card is not what the founder receives
*panel-query — VIEW C: email query compose (#qview-email) — functionality · effort S · found on review*

- **Gap** — QueryPage.tsx:170 flattens the two fields into one string — `const message = [subject, "", body].join("\n")` — and posts it as the `questions` payload (:171). The server never treats it as an email: buildQueryEmail (outbox.ts:229-239) mints its OWN subject, `Action needed: a few questions about ${deckName}`, and wraps the payload in its own greeting and sign-off — `${greeting}\n\nThanks for submitting ${deckName} to the programme. Before we can complete the review, our team needs a little more detail:\n\n${questions}\n\n...`. The founder therefore gets: a subject the operator never wrote and never saw; the operator's subject line buried as plain text in the middle of the body; and two stacked greetings ('Hi Ananya,' from the server, then 'Dear Founder,' from the composed body at shared/queries.ts:54). The file's own header comment at QueryPage.tsx:13-14 claims 'what is on screen is what the founder receives', which is false. The Subject input on this screen is decorative.
- **Prototype** — panel-query.html:276 (`<div class="fl">Subject</div><input type="text" value="Clarification requested on your pitchdeck submission">`) and :277-288 (the Body textarea) — in the prototype these two fields ARE the email
- **Repository** — src/client/routes/QueryPage.tsx:13-14, :170-171; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:528-543; src/server/email/outbox.ts:224-239
- **Fix** — Pass subject and body as separate fields on POST /decks/:id/queries and have the route use them verbatim (keeping buildQueryEmail only as the default when the caller sends none), or drop the Subject input and show the server-generated subject read-only so the screen stops promising editorial control it does not have.

### F0223 · `P1` · Bulk upload discards the operator's program, cohort and workspace sector — every bulk deck lands untagged and is forced Incomplete on a sector the operator already knows
*upload — functionality · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — On a bulk upload the repo sends nothing but the PDFs. Each deck is stored with sector = NULL, program_id = NULL and cohort_id = NULL, so (a) it is invisible to every program/cohort-scoped filter, report and shortlist floor even though the operator was standing in an active program context (the same context ConfigPage's 'Applies to' card and the single-upload form both use), and (b) because `sector` is one of the five required intake columns, any deck whose PDF does not state a sector is marked Incomplete and pushed into the founder-query loop for a value the workspace already holds. The prototype explicitly rules this out: sector comes from setup context and is never scanned. The repo's own bulk help text (UploadPage.tsx:452-456) even says the AI reads 'name, email, phone and city' — omitting sector — while the server still requires it.
- **Prototype** — VC_Final_files_AISJ_VC_Superuser_V6_html/panel-upload.html — `#up-results` `.up-results-note`: "Sector is taken from your workspace setup context (<b id='up-results-sector'>FinTech</b>) — not scanned from the deck. Founder name, email, phone and city are extracted from each deck on upload"; `renderUpResults` (scratchpad/vc_up.js) prints `e.sector` from the module-level `var UP_SECTOR='FinTech'`, never from the deck. The single-upload method also carries a Cohort select.
- **Repository** — src/client/routes/UploadPage.tsx:172-190 (submitBulk appends only `files` — no programId, cohortId or sector); src/client/api.ts:324-326; src/server/routes/decks.ts:1205-1256 (bulk handler reads only `form.getAll("files")` and calls `storeDeck(c, file, {})` at :1240); src/server/routes/decks.ts:1005-1028 (storeDeck writes sector/program_id/cohort_id as NULL when meta is empty); src/shared/intake.ts:23-29 + :106-116 (sector is a REQUIRED intake field, so a NULL sector is a missingIntakeField)
- **Fix** — Append the active `programId`/`cohortId` and the context sector to the bulk FormData; read them in the bulk handler and pass them through `storeDeck`'s meta; default `sector` from the program/cohort context inside `mergeIntakeDetails` so extraction only has to fill it when no context sector exists.

### F0227 · `P1` · Sector is treated as an AI-extracted required field that can mark a deck Incomplete, directly contradicting the prototype's "Sector is taken from your workspace setup context — not scanned from the deck"
*upload / #up-wizard (metadata form) + #up-results — functionality · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — The prototype guarantees sector from setup context; the repo asks Claude to read it off the deck, lets the uploader type any free-text string, and marks the deck Incomplete (which triggers the founder-clarification email via src/server/resubmit.ts) when neither supplies it. The workspace already holds the answer — the Set up wizard manages a sector list (src/client/routes/SetupWizard.tsx:352-375) and each program carries a sector (api.ts:677 `ProgramView.sector`) — but the Upload screen ignores both, so decks are sent back to founders for a field the prototype says is never asked of them, and free text fragments the Sector column that DashboardPage.tsx:408 and the sectorMix analytics (src/shared/analytics.ts:193-198) group on.
- **Prototype** — panel-upload.html:322 — "Sector is taken from your workspace setup context (<b id=\"up-results-sector\">FinTech</b>) — not scanned from the deck. Founder name, email, phone and city are extracted from each deck on upload"; panel-upload.html:195 renders Sector as a `<select class="up-select">` of configured sectors, not free text; inc_up.js:28 `var UP_SECTOR='FinTech'` and inc_up.js:40 `upExtract()` always returns `sector: UP_SECTOR`, so the Sector cell is never "not captured" and inc_up.js:41 `upDetailsComplete` can never fail on sector.
- **Repository** — src/shared/intake.ts:24-30 (sector is in REQUIRED_INTAKE_FIELDS) and :112 (`if (!clean(d.sector)) missing.push("sector")` → deck Incomplete); src/server/ai/evaluate.ts:248-251 and :339 (the model is told to return "the startup's sector exactly as stated in the deck — return null for anything the …"); src/client/routes/UploadPage.tsx:329-331 (Sector is a free-text `<input>` with placeholder "e.g. FinTech", no default from the workspace) and :47-53 (sector sits in DETAIL_COLUMNS alongside the genuinely-extracted founder fields)
- **Fix** — Default sector on the Upload form from the active program/workspace context and render it as a select over the configured sectors; drop sector from REQUIRED_INTAKE_FIELDS' Incomplete trigger (or fall back to the context value before computing missingIntakeFields) and stop prompting the model for it.

## Design system & chrome

### F0349 · `P0` · Set/change password and forgot-password have no client or server counterpart
*global-profile-menu (.prof-menu) — functionality · effort L · severity adjusted*

- **Gap** — A user cannot change their own password or request a reset link anywhere in the product; the prototype exposes both from the top bar and from the signed-out state.
- **Prototype** — `_topnav.html` `#prof-pwtoggle` → `profTogglePw()` with current/new/confirm inputs and `profSavePw()`; `#prof-fp-toggle` → `profSendReset('')` with an email field and Send reset link (also in the signed-out `#prof-out-view`).
- **Repository** — NONE — src/server/routes/auth.ts only has login (verifyPassword at :43); grep for forgot/reset-link/changePassword across src/server and src/client returns nothing. Passwords are only issued as admin temp passwords (src/server/routes/users.ts:252-256).
- **Fix** — Add POST /auth/change-password and POST /auth/forgot-password (token + email), plus the two forms in the profile menu.
- **Reviewer** — Confirmed and larger than claimed. Prototype side verified: `#prof-pwtoggle` → profTogglePw() with prof-pw-cur/new/conf + profSavePw(), and `#prof-fp-toggle` → profSendReset('') with an email field, plus the duplicate `#prof-fp2-*` pair inside the signed-out `#prof-out-view`; the whole block is pres

### F0350 · `P1` · The whole page scrolls in the repo; the prototype's fixed-frame shell (pinned panel toolbar, pinned footer stat+legend bar, 278px right rail) has no counterpart
*global-app-shell-layout (.view/.ab/.mn) + global-panel-toolbar (.su-tb/.su-foot) + .rp right pane — layout · effort L · found on review*

- **Gap** — In the prototype the chrome is fixed and only the data region moves: the page title/subtitle/Filter/Export strip is a white bordered bar pinned to the top of the panel, and the count + colour legend is a white bordered bar pinned to the bottom, with the table scrolling between them (and, where used, a 278px right pane beside it). In the repo nothing is pinned — the header, table and legend are one long scrolling column on the page background, the toolbar disappears as soon as the user scrolls a long table, and the legend is only reachable by scrolling past every row. This is the single most-repeated layout in both editions (10 of 22 incubator panels and 11 of 30 VC panels use the su- frame outright, and every remaining panel uses the same overflow:hidden + inner-scroll pattern), so it affects essentially every screen.
- **Prototype** — Incubator_Final_files_AISJ_IC_SuserV11_HTM/_style.css: `.view{height:100vh;flex-direction:column;overflow:hidden}` → `.ab{display:flex;flex:1;overflow:hidden}` → `.mn{flex:1;display:flex;flex-direction:column;overflow:hidden}`, and 21 of 22 panel roots are `<div id="panel-*" style="display:none;flex:1;flex-direction:column;overflow:hidden">`. Scrolling is confined to an inner region: `.su-scroll{flex:1;overflow:auto}` / `.dp{flex:1;overflow-y:auto;padding:12px 16px}`. Above it `.su-tb{padding:11px 18px;background:var(--surface);border-bottom:1px solid var(--stone-dk);flex-shrink:0}` holds title+sub+toolbar buttons; below it `.su-foot{flex-shrink:0;padding:10px 18px;border-top:1px solid var(--stone);background:var(--surface)}` holds `.su-foot-stat` (count) on the left and `.su-legend` (colour dots) on the right — see panel-forsignup.html, panel-incuration.html, panel-alldecks.html. `.rp{width:278px;min-width:278px;border-left:1px solid var(--stone-dk);overflow-y:auto;background:var(--surface)}` is the shell's right rail.
- **Repository** — src/client/components/AppShell.tsx:58 `<main className="min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto">` — the entire routed page is the scroll container, and the shell offers no right-rail slot. src/client/routes/StagePage.tsx:448 `<div className="flex flex-col gap-5 p-5">` — title, subtitle and Export scroll away with the table; StagePage.tsx:553-562 renders the legend as an ordinary flow element BENEATH the table instead of in a pinned footer, and the row count is a `<Badge tone="info">` beside the title (StagePage.tsx:456) rather than a `.su-foot-stat` line.
- **Fix** — Give the shell a fixed frame: make <main> `overflow-hidden` and introduce a shared PanelFrame (sticky bordered header on --surface holding title/subtitle/toolbar, a `flex-1 overflow-auto` body, and an optional pinned footer taking the stat line + legend), plus an optional right-rail slot. Then convert StagePage / CallsPage / the report screens onto it.

*global-branding-application — functionality · effort M · verified*

- **Gap** — An admin can set a wordmark, tagline and accent colour and nothing anywhere in the app changes — the values are written to config and never read by the shell.

- **Fix** — Read branding in AppShell/ThemeProvider, write `--accent` (and friends) onto the root element, and feed wordmark/tagline into Logo.
- **Reviewer** — Confirmed, and the claim understates the gap. Verified _scripts.js:2141-2148 brSet() writes `document.documentElement.style.setProperty(token, hex)`, brSetText():2162 / brLogoText():2164 rewrite #brand-a/#brand-s/#brand-tag, brLogoImg():2178-2192 swaps #brand-mark + #brand-textwrap for #brand-img, a

### F0352 · `P1` · The prototype's olive primary family has no token in the repo at all
*global-colour-tokens — visual · effort M · verified*

### F0357 · `P1` · The whole UI runs ~20-40% larger and looser than the prototype's dense console scale
*global-typography-density — visual · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Every measurable dimension is inflated against the prototype: sidebar 240 vs 190px (+26%), nav label 14 vs 11.5px (+22%), section label 11 vs 9px (+22%), page title 20 vs 14px (+43%), page subtitle 14 vs 11px (+27%), toolbar button 12 vs 11px, avatar 32 vs 27px. The prototype is deliberately a dense information console — a Super User's full sidebar fits above the fold at 190px/11.5px and the su-tb strip is only 11px tall in padding — whereas the repo reads as a roomy web app. Given the client's 'exactly match the way it should look', this is a systematic divergence visible on every screen, not a per-screen nit, and it is what forces the sidebar overflow that the Aug-2026 issue 10 collapsible-sections change worked around.
- **Prototype** — _style.css: `.sb{width:190px;min-width:190px}`; `.si{padding:6px 12px;font-size:11.5px}`; `.sbl{font-size:9px;letter-spacing:.07em}`; `.an{height:54px}`; `.nav-av{width:27px;height:27px;font-size:10px}`; `.su-tb{padding:11px 18px}`; `.su-tb-title{font-size:14px;font-weight:600}`; `.su-tb-sub{font-size:11px}`; `.tbb{font-size:11px;padding:5px 11px}`; `.sc{padding:11px 13px}`; `.sp{font-size:10px;padding:2px 7px}`.
- **Repository** — src/client/components/AppShell.tsx:36 `hidden w-60 …` (240px sidebar); Sidebar.tsx:92 `px-2 py-1.5 text-sm` (14px nav items); src/client/index.css:102-107 `.u-label{font-size:0.6875rem}` (11px section labels); Topbar.tsx:36 `h-14` (56px) with an `h-8 w-8` (32px) avatar at :87-92; StagePage.tsx:450-452 `text-xl font-semibold` title (20px) + `text-sm` subtitle (14px) inside `p-5`; Button.tsx:14 sm = `h-8 px-3 text-xs`; KpiTile.tsx:31 `px-4 py-3.5`.
- **Fix** — Introduce a density scale in index.css (a base 11.5-13px UI size with matching spacing tokens), set the sidebar to 190px and the topbar to 54px, and re-map the shared components (Sidebar item, Button sizes, page title/subtitle in StagePage/CallsPage/ReportShell, KpiTile, Badge) onto it.

The nearest surface is the dashboard activity feed (api.ts:165, DashboardPage.tsx:172), which reads pipeline_events only. No admin audit screen exists.

The repo instead made "founder" a password role, then built no way to create such a user (no self-registration endpoint, admin creation explicitly excludes the role, no provisioning at send_signup) and no code/link sign-in. So every founder screen is dead in production, and the shortlist email instructs the founder to do something with no link to click and no account to sign in with. Partial mitigation: src/pipeline/incubator.ts:127-133 also lets admin/superuser fire complete_signup, so staff can push the deck through on the founder's behalf — a workaround, not the specified workflow. If the parent considers the founder portal beyond-prototype scope, this is still at minimum a P1 broken email/workflow.
- **Prototype** — panels/Incubator_Final_files_AISJ_IC_SuserV11_HTM/_rest.html:1389-1405 — #fp-ov > #fp-login "Respond to evaluation questions": Registered email (#fp-email) + Access code (#fp-code, "6-digit code from your email") → fpAuth(), i.e. the prototype authenticates founders with an emailed access code, not a password account. Same #fp-login exists in the VC superuser _rest.html. panel-forsignup.html shows the staff-side "For Sign up" board with a "Sign-up status" column (Initiated / In progress / Completed) that the founder is supposed to drive.
- **Repository** — src/shared/nav.ts:121-124 (four founder screens, portal:"founder") + src/client/App.tsx:99-101 + src/client/routes/FounderPortal.tsx:183-211 (FounderSignupPage → transitionDeck "complete_signup"); src/shared/roles.ts:206-212 comment says "founders are external self-registrants" and creatableStaffRoles() FILTERS OUT founder; src/server/routes/users.ts:241 rejects any non-staff role, and users.ts:256 is the ONLY `INSERT INTO users` in src/ (verified by grep) and is admin-only; the sole founder account in existence is the seeded migrations/0002_seed.sql:50 `inc_founder`; src/server/email/outbox.ts:260-271 buildSignupEmail says "Complete your sign-up in the founder portal to move into onboarding" with NO url and NO credential (contrast the resubmit mail, outbox.ts:346, which does embed a tokenized link).
- **Fix** — Either (a) provision a founder user + emailed one-time access code at POST /decks/:id/send-signup and add a code/token sign-in for the founder portal (mirrors #fp-login), or (b) convert founder-signup to a tokenized public page like /resubmit/:token and put that link in buildSignupEmail. Also remove the "external self-registrants" comment or build the registration it promises.

The screen states the opposite in two sentences, so the defect is invisible to the operator sending it.

- **Fix** — Move message generation inside the send loop — call `buildQueryMessage(deck.name, areasNeedingResponse(deck))` per deck and post that — and change the composer for a multi-select into a per-recipient preview (or an editable template with per-founder area substitution) rather than one shared textarea.

### F0488 · `P2` · A signed-in user can never see which email account they are signed in as, and the plan pill's "set by your subscription" explanation is gone
*prof-menu identity rows vs repo /app/account — data-columns · effort S · found on review*

- **Gap** — Two concrete losses against the spec: (1) the account identifier — the prototype's "Username" row — is unreachable in the product, which matters precisely because the repo's login model is email+password and users are invited under an address an admin typed; (2) the prototype deliberately explains that the plan is subscription-controlled, which is what stops an admin hunting for a plan control that isn't there. Fixing (1) needs the email added to the session/me payload, not just the page.
- **Prototype** — panels/Incubator_Final_files_AISJ_IC_SuserV11_HTM/_topnav.html — `<div class="prof-row"><div class="prof-lbl">Username</div><div class="prof-val">priya.sharma@company.com</div></div>`, and the plan row `#prof-plan-pill` (crown + plan name + lock icon) whose onclick=profPlanLocked() reveals `#prof-plan-note`: "Your plan is set by your subscription and can't be changed here." (_scripts.js:3243).
- **Repository** — src/client/routes/AccountPage.tsx:52-57 — the rows are Name / Platform role / Workspace / Edition; the email is never rendered anywhere on the page, and the plan appears only as a bare `<Badge tone="amber">{PLAN_LABELS[plan]} plan</Badge>` at :78 with no lock affordance and no explanatory note. The session principal does not even carry the email: AuthProvider.tsx:12-23 AuthUser is {id,name,initials,role,edition,title} and src/server/routes/auth.ts:15-31 toSessionUser omits it.
- **Fix** — Include `email` in SessionUser/toSessionUser and AuthUser, render it as a "Username" row on AccountPage, and add the locked plan pill plus the "set by your subscription" note next to the plan badge.

- **Fix** — Turn the name cell into a controlled text input and include `name` in the updateWeights payload; the server path already exists.

### F0560 · `P1` · The prototype dispatches every selected deck to EVERY selected member (deck × member); the repo can only give a deck ONE assignee, so it round-robins instead
*assign ("Submit") — functionality · effort L · found on review*

- **Gap** — The design's core assignment semantics are inverted. In the prototype, ticking 3 decks and 4 members creates 12 evaluations — every member evaluates every deck, which is what makes the pipeline's multi-juror score column and the AI-vs-jury drift comparison meaningful. The repo splits 3 decks across 4 members (3 evaluations, one evaluator per deck), because `decks.assigned_to` is a single foreign key. This is not a UI difference: rebuilding the Submit screen as specified is impossible without a deck↔evaluator join table, so it is a prerequisite for the P0 in claim 1 rather than a follow-up to it.
- **Prototype** — VC SU _scripts.js:1144-1157 asConfirm() — `selectedDecks.forEach(d => members.forEach(mem => rows.push({...})))`, i.e. N×M dispatch rows; renderAs4() at :1188 states the contract in the UI: "<strong>N</strong> decks × <strong>M</strong> jury members = <strong>N×M</strong> evaluations". The pipeline panels corroborate the many-evaluators-per-deck model: jpRowDefault (:1966-1996) renders a `d.jurors` array with a per-juror score row each.
- **Repository** — src/client/routes/AssignPage.tsx:70-76 (`selectedDecks.map((deck, i) => ({ deck, member: selectedMembers[i % selectedMembers.length] }))`) and the acknowledging comment at AssignPage.tsx:20-22 ("…because a deck carries one assignee"); the constraint is in the schema — migrations/0001_init.sql:64 `assigned_to TEXT REFERENCES users (id)` (one column), written by src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:296 `UPDATE decks SET … assigned_to = ?`.
- **Fix** — Introduce a `deck_assignments (deck_id, evaluator_id, assigned_at, deadline_at, instructions)` table, make the assign endpoint accept a member LIST, and derive `assigned_to`/`assigned_at` from it for backward compatibility. Then panel 4's "N × M = X evaluations" and the results table's one-row-per-dispatch layout follow naturally.

### F0561 · `P1` · A VC deck can be set to status 'incomplete', but the VC pipeline defines no such stage — the deck becomes a dead end with a raw lowercase label and zero available actions
*assign ("Submit") / VC pipeline — functionality · vc · effort S · found on review*

- **Gap** — When the AI cannot score a VC deck, `computeResult` parks it at `status='incomplete'`. `getStage('vc','incomplete')` returns undefined, so (a) every screen shows the literal lowercase string "incomplete" instead of a stage label, (b) `allowedTransitions` finds nothing, so the deck has zero action buttons anywhere, and (c) nothing in vc.ts can move it back — the incubator's `incomplete → uploaded` resubmit transition (incubator.ts:65) has no VC twin. The deck is permanently stuck, which is the functional half of the incomplete/Query loop the Submit screen is supposed to drive. The auditor reported the missing UI (claim 3) but not that the underlying stage does not exist.
- **Prototype** — VC SU panel-assign.html `#as-incomplete` + _scripts.js:1112 asShowIncomplete() / :1131 asSendToQuery() / :1108 asIncompleteDecks(), and the seed rows at :858-859 (`AgriChain`, `PayRoute` with `incomplete:true, missing:'…'`) — the VC edition's prototype explicitly models incomplete decks and their route back out via Query.
- **Repository** — src/pipeline/vc.ts:9-26 — the VC `stages` array has no `incomplete` entry (the incubator's is at src/pipeline/incubator.ts:18); src/server/ai/evaluate.ts:417-420 `computeResult` returns `status: "incomplete"` with no edition check and evaluate.ts:721 mails the founder about it; src/server/routes/decks.ts:139-141 `statusLabel` falls back to the raw id when getStage() misses; src/client/routes/QueryPage.tsx:36 lists `"incomplete"` for the VC edition.
- **Fix** — Add an `incomplete` stage to vc.ts plus the resubmit transition back to `uploaded`/`analyst_scoring`, mirroring incubator.ts:58-70.

### F0579 · `P1` · The prototype's "Submit forward" keeps the row on the pipeline with a Submitted pill + date; the repo's equivalent transition moves the deck off the screen entirely
*jurypipeline / partnerpipeline — functionality · vc · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — In the repo, acting on a row immediately changes the deck's stage, and because each screen filters on a fixed stage list the row vanishes the moment you act on it. The prototype's model is a persistent tracking table ("Track every deck through jury evaluation") in which submitting stamps a date and a Submitted pill and THEN asks where to send it. This is why the prototype needs a Submitted-date column (claim 8), a two-state Status pill (claim 9), a Submit-to column (claim 7) and a footer legend counting shortlisted/rejected/in-progress (claim 10) — those four reported gaps are all symptoms of this one workflow difference, and fixing them individually without it will not reproduce the screen.
- **Prototype** — _scripts.js:2117-2126 jpAction() — for pfx 'jp'/'pp' the `submit` option sets `jpData[i].submitted = true; jpData[i].subDate = jpToday();` then re-renders IN PLACE and toasts "✓ Submitted — choose a role to submit to". jpRowAssoc (:2019-2024) then flips the Status pill to Submitted, fills the Submitted date and swaps the ninth cell from an em-dash to jpSubmitToSelect(). The row never leaves the table.
- **Repository** — src/pipeline/vc.ts:47-56 — `submit_core_scores` (analyst_scoring → associate_review) and `shortlist_to_partner` (associate_review → partner_review); src/client/routes/StagePage.tsx:600 jurypipeline `statuses: ["analyst_scoring", "associate_review"]` and :610 partnerpipeline `statuses: ["partner_review"]`.
- **Fix** — Either widen the two VC configs' `statuses` so decided decks stay listed (as the incubator jurypipeline already does at StagePage.tsx:672 with shortlisted/rejected), or model submission as a per-deck flag distinct from the stage move.

### F0663 · `P1` · The 13 core areas carry no per-area AI extraction prompt and no clarification-question set
*Core Parameters / Evaluate → parameter detail — data-model · vc · effort L · found on review*

The per-area extraction prompt — the thing that makes the AI's 13 scores auditable and fund-tunable — collapses to one workspace-wide system prompt plus an autogenerated sentence, and the five clarification questions per area that the prototype fires 'when signals are weak' have no storage, no seed and no editor. This is the same root cause as the rubric-band finding (claim 9) but a distinct missing field: even if the five bands were added, the prompt and the question bank would still be absent.

If signals are weak, missing, or contradictory, trigger the clarification questions for this area.') AND a five-item `criteria` array of clarification questions. :577-600 `evOpenParam(i)` renders the detail card as 'Evaluation prompt' (with Save / Configure buttons), 'AI clarification questions (asked when signals are weak)', then 'Rubric anchors'. Spec vc.html §6.1: 'Each area is scored 0–10, has a five-band rubric (§7), an AI-extraction prompt, and a weight defined in-file.'
- **Repository** — migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:16-18 states the intent plainly — the new `prompt` column is 'NULL for core areas, which fall back to name + weight'. src/server/routes/config.ts:151-190 `PUT /parameters` is the only core-parameter write and accepts nothing but `weight` and `name` (:174-178), so a core area's prompt can never be set or edited. src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:443 papers over the absence with a generated string: `{param.prompt ?? `Score ${param.name} from 0 to 10 against the rubric anchors below.`}`. There is one global prompt instead (config.ts:331-344 `PUT /ai-prompt` → org_settings.ai_system_prompt). - **Fix** — Add `prompt` seeding for the 13 core rows and a `parameter_questions` (or JSON column) table for the five clarification questions per area; extend `PUT /config/parameters` to accept prompt/questions alongside weight, and render them in the EvaluatePage parameter detail panel where the anchors already appear.

### F0664 · `P1` · The AI suggested score is never pre-filled as the human's starting value — every untouched parameter is submitted as a deliberate 5.0
*Evaluate (EvaluatePage) — scoring · effort S · found on review*

- **Gap** — There is no override semantics at all: the human always starts from a flat 5 regardless of what the AI found, and an evaluator who opens a deck, writes a remark and clicks Save records a full, submitted, weighted evaluation of 5.0 across every parameter. That evaluation then feeds the deck's human average, the AI-vs-human drift report and the pipeline ranking as if it were real scoring. Combined with the absent draft state and completeness gate (claim 5), nothing in the product distinguishes a scored deck from an opened one.
- **Prototype** — spec §2: "the platform's AI pre-populates a suggested score (0–10) for each of the 13 standard evaluation areas … Human evaluators then review and override scores". spec §7: "AI supplies a suggested value; the human can override." spec §10: "AI pre-fills a suggested score using each parameter's prompt."
- **Repository** — src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:109 — `setValues(Object.fromEntries(allScored.map((p) => [p.key, 5])))` on every deck selection, before loadDeckData runs; :86-97 loads the AI breakdown into a SEPARATE `aiScores` map that is only displayed, never merged into `values`; :125 and :143 then post `allScored.map(p => ({key: p.key, value: values[p.key] ?? 0}))` — all 13 core + up-to-3 additional, every time.
- **Fix** — Seed `values` from the AI suggestion once loadDeckData resolves (falling back to 5 only where the AI produced nothing), and track which parameters the human actually touched so the submit gate in claim 5 has something to check.

### F0665 · `P1` · Score inputs are locked to whole numbers; the spec and prototype both use 0.5 steps
*Evaluate / EvalScorecard — scoring · effort S · found on review*

- **Gap** — An evaluator physically cannot enter 7.5, which the spec's band table treats as "Strong" and which the repo's own seeded human scores use (migrations/0024 stores 9.5, 8.5, 7.5 across five decks). The report renders those half-steps but the scorecard cannot reproduce them, so re-opening and re-saving a seeded evaluation silently rounds every half-step away.
- **Prototype** — spec §7: "Per-area score: integer/half-step 0–10 (step 0.5)". live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:3733, :3767 and :4288 — the active scoring inputs are emitted with `step="0.5"`.
- **Repository** — src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx:248 (core parameters) and :306 (additional parameters) — both range inputs are `min={0} max={10} step={1}`. These are the only two score inputs in the component.
- **Fix** — Change step to 0.5 on both inputs in EvalScorecard.tsx and widen the value readout column (currently w-5, sized for one digit).

### F0666 · `P1` · Scoring is bound to neither a role nor a gate — any VC evaluator can score any deal in any of the three scoring stages
*Evaluate / Submit (VC) — authorization · vc · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Nothing binds a role's lens to its gate. A partner can score at analyst_scoring, an analyst at partner_review, and (per the corrected claim 2) an IC member scores their IC lens during partner review — the one stage the spec reserves for the partner lens. Combined with the absence of an Assignment record, there is also no per-deck ownership on the VC side at all, so any evaluator can score any deal in the funnel. This is the enforcement half of §8.4 that the auditor's claim 3 (the missing Assign SCREEN and entity) and claim 7 (the non-stage-aware REPORT) each touch but neither states: even with the existing schema, the server permits wrong-role-at-wrong-gate writes today.
- **Prototype** — Spec vc.html §8.4: 'at each gate the current role's own parameters are editable; upstream roles' parameters are shown as read-only reference ("completed"); downstream sections are hidden until reached', and §5: 'Assignment links a deck to an evaluator and records the role lens and the pipeline stage; it gates whether a user gets an editable vs read-only workspace at that gate.' The prototype enforces this by opening the report from a specific pipeline panel with a specific role lens — e.g. _scripts.js:2134 opens it from panel-icpipeline with `role:'jury', roleName:'IC Member'` and the icScored flag, so only the IC block is editable there.
- **Repository** — src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:50 `const VC_SCORING_STAGES = ["analyst_scoring", "associate_review", "partner_review"]` is ONE flat list applied to every VC role at :344-346, and the per-deck ownership check immediately above it is incubator-only: :339-342 `if (user.role === "jury" && deck.assigned_to !== user.id)`. requireRole at :325-333 admits analyst, associate, partner and ic_member equally. On the client, src/client/routes/VcEvaluatePage.tsx:60-63 `rows = decks.filter(d => SCORING_STAGES.includes(d.statusId))` applies no assignment filter and no role↔stage pairing, so every evaluator sees every deal in all three stages.
- **Fix** — Derive the permitted (role, stage) pairs from src/pipeline/vc.ts rather than a flat stage list — e.g. analyst↔analyst_scoring, associate↔associate_review, partner↔partner_review, ic_member↔ic_review — reject a score whose role does not own the deal's current stage, and filter the Evaluate queue by the same pairing plus the assignment once it exists.

### F0667 · `P1` · Per-parameter evaluator remarks cannot be entered anywhere — the column exists, the UI never writes it
*Evaluate / Submit (VC) — EvalScorecard — missing-input · vc · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — A human evaluator can attach one note to the whole deck but cannot say anything about an individual parameter — the exact artefact the prototype's expander collects and the report replays as an upstream role's reference. Because `scores.comment` is populated only by the AI path (ai/evaluate.ts), the report's per-score tooltip (EvaluationReport.tsx:97) can only ever show AI text, never a colleague's reasoning. This is a pure 'API exists, no UI' gap: the column, the request type and the server write are all in place.
- **Prototype** — live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:4295 — every core-parameter row expands to `<div class="jr-myrem"><label>My remarks for this parameter</label><textarea … oninput="jrRem(k,this.value)">`; :4497 `window.jrRem=function(k,val){ myRemarks[curName][k]=val; }`; :4502 `jrCustomRem` does the same for each additional parameter; :4382 the read-only `roAddl` block replays an upstream role's per-parameter remark. Spec vc.html §5: 'Evaluation 1───∞ EvaluationRemark (one per parameter, optional)' and §12 `evaluation_remarks(evaluation_id, parameter_id, remark)`; §13 `PATCH /evaluations/:id save draft (scores + remarks)'.
- **Repository** — The storage and the API both exist: migrations/0001_init.sql:92 `scores.comment TEXT`; src/client/api.ts:399-403 `HumanScoreInput { key; value; comment?: string }`; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:371 `clean.push({ …, comment: s.comment ?? null })`. Nothing ever supplies it. src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx renders each parameter row with only a range input (:243-256 core, :300-311 additional) and offers exactly one whole-evaluation textarea at :324-332 ('Remarks (optional)'); src/client/routes/VcEvaluatePage.tsx:108 and src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:125,:143 all build the payload as `allScored.map((p) => ({ key: p.key, value: values[p.key] ?? 0 }))` with no comment. `grep -n comment` across those three files returns only READS of the AI's comment (EvalScorecard.tsx:230,:288).
- **Fix** — Add a per-row remark textarea (collapsed expander) to EvalScorecard for both the core and additional tables, thread it through `onChangeRemark(key, text)` into the `comment` field the payload already supports, and surface it in EvaluationReport's row expander instead of the title tooltip.

### F0668 · `P1` · The "Jury score" that ranks the pipeline averages every human evaluator, not the jury
*Jury Pipeline / Intro calls / Sign up Pipeline (StagePage "Jury score" column) — scoring · incubator · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — A Program Associate's or Program Manager's or Admin's evaluation is folded into the number displayed and sorted as the jury's verdict, and the deck's decision score inherits the same contamination. Because the repo also has no assignments table (claim 4), there is no role recorded on the evaluation either — the only role available is the evaluator's current user role, which nothing in the query consults. I found no meeting note or issue-log entry that chose this behaviour deliberately.
- **Prototype** — spec §7: "Jury aggregation: across all jury evaluations of a deck, average the per-parameter scores (and the composite). This average is what ranks the pipeline." spec §12 aggregation views: "deck_jury_score = avg of jury evaluations.composite for a deck" and "deck_pipeline_rank = order by deck_jury_score within a program".
- **Repository** — src/server/routes/decks.ts:58 — `(SELECT AVG(e.weighted_total) FROM evaluations e WHERE e.deck_id = d.id AND e.evaluator_id IS NOT NULL) AS human_avg` — no join to users, no role filter. decks.ts:236 exposes it as `juryScore`; decks.ts:197-200 feeds the same value into `decisionScore(ai, [human_avg])` as the deck's decision score. src/client/routes/StagePage.tsx:88 labels the column "Jury score" and it appears on jurypipeline, pmpipeline, introcalls and incuration (lines 602, 612, 677, 694, 713).
- **Fix** — Filter human_avg to jury-lens evaluations (join users and restrict to the edition's jury role — jury for incubator, ic_member for VC), or keep the all-hands average but rename the column and stop using it as the jury aggregate in decisionScore.

### F0669 · `P1` · No credit_ledger — credits are a bare counter, so per-deck spend, usage history and 'of N purchased' have no backing data
*buy credits / admin console → Credits & billing — schema-and-api · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Nothing in the product can answer 'which decks consumed my credits, when, and what did I pay'. Without a ledger there is no 'of 50 purchased' denominator, no 'used this month', no per-deck usage rows, no purchase or refund record, and no invoice source — and the refund path in decks.ts:1169 silently mutates a counter with no audit. This is one of §12's 21 tables and one of §13's 14 endpoints, and the auditor's schema and API-surface findings do not mention either.
- **Prototype** — Spec §12 lists `credit_ledger(id, org_id ⟶ organizations, delta int, reason[trial_grant|deck_evaluated|purchase], deck_id ⟶ decks nullable, created_at)`; §13 lists `GET /orgs/:id/credits` → 'balance + ledger'; §10 fixes the metering rule 'one credit per deck evaluated; new orgs start with trial credits (e.g. 3)'. The console section renders it: live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/admin/s-bl.html shows 'Credits remaining 47 of 50 purchased', 'Used this month 3 · ₹2,997 consumed', and a 'Usage history' list of per-deck rows ('GreenGrid Energy — pitchdeck evaluation | 1 credit · ₹999 · 4 Jun 2026') above 'Buy more credits / Download invoice / Upgrade plan'.
- **Repository** — `grep -rn credit_ledger` across the repo returns nothing. The entire credit model is one integer: migrations/0001_init.sql:18 `org_settings.credits_balance`. src/server/routes/config.ts:372 POST /credits and :390 POST /credits/purchase both just UPDATE that counter (`credits_balance = credits_balance + ?`), and there is no GET that returns anything but the scalar (config.ts:99 /summary → creditsBalance, config.ts:122 / → creditsBalance). src/client/routes/BuyCreditsPage.tsx has no history, invoice or 'purchased' section — grep for history/transaction/ledger/Recent in it returns nothing. src/server/routes/decks.ts:1169 already reasons about giving a credit back on AI failure ('A terminal failure gave the credit back; re-driving spends it again') but has nowhere to record either event.

### F0670 · `P1` · Runtime scoring bands are 4 with the wrong cutoffs and wrong labels, not the spec's 5
*cross-cutting (every score badge, matrix cell and pipeline bar) — scoring · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — Every band chip in the product reports a different band from the one the spec defines: 7.5 is 'Strong' per §1/§7 but renders 'Moderate'; 9.5 is 'Exceptional' but renders 'Strong'; 1.5 is 'Insufficient' but renders 'Absent'. Because §7 says the band index drives colour coding, the colour of every score in every matrix, badge and pipeline bar is off too, and the AI is told the wrong anchors (src/server/ai/evaluate.ts:313-317 builds the band list straight from these four rubric_anchors rows). This is the RUNTIME half of the rubric problem and is separately fixable from the auditor's claim 10, which reports only the missing per-parameter band descriptor STORAGE and mentions the four-band split as an aside without scoring it as a gap.
- **Prototype** — Spec §1 'Key enums' fixes it: 'Scoring bands (applied per area, 0–10): 9–10 Exceptional · 7–8 Strong · 5–6 Moderate · 3–4 Weak · 0–2 Insufficient.' §7 restates it as a function — 'Band mapping (band(v)): v≥9 → Exceptional(0), v≥7 → Strong(1), v≥5 → Moderate(2), v≥3 → Weak(3), else Insufficient(4). Band index also drives colour coding.' §12's parameter_rubric_bands pins the same five as its band_label enum [9–10|7–8|5–6|3–4|0–2]. The prototype implements it verbatim at AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:3632 `function band(v){ return v>=9?0:v>=7?1:v>=5?2:v>=3?3:4; }`, and admin/s-rb.html calls it 'the BRD five-band scale'.
- **Repository** — src/shared/scoring.ts:19-26 `signalTag`: `if (value >= 8) return 'strong'; if (value >= 5) return 'moderate'; if (value >= 2) return 'weak'; return 'absent';` — four bands, different thresholds, and neither 'Exceptional' nor 'Insufficient' exists as a label anywhere (`grep -rni 'exceptional|insufficient' src/` finds nothing). migrations/0002_seed.sql:5-9 seeds rubric_anchors to match: strong 8-10, moderate 5-7, weak 2-4, absent 0-1. The same four-way split is baked into the token names (index.css:28-31 --color-signal-strong/moderate/weak/absent) and into the analytics band accounting (src/shared/analytics.ts:345 'Signal band index … (0=absent … 3=strong)').

*§7 Jury aggregation — wrong-formula · incubator · effort M*

### F0748 · `P2` · Zero-weight composite returns 0 instead of falling back to the AI value
*§7 Scoring & Aggregation — wrong-fallback · incubator · effort S*

- **Gap** — An org that zeroes every core weight (reachable — config.ts:172 permits weight 0 on every parameter and never checks the sum) gets a composite of 0 for every deck rather than the AI value, which reads as "all decks scored zero" rather than "unweighted".

- **Repository** — src/shared/scoring.ts:13-14 `if (totalWeight === 0) return 0;`
- **Fix** — Pass the AI composite into weightedTotal as the zero-weight fallback.

This is a data-surface defect independent of the missing batch controls (claim 2): it applies equally to the SU variant A, which has no batch bar but the same pre-assignment list, and it means the Upload→Evaluate→Assign stage hand-off the prototype depicts exists on no screen at all.

The SU variant A uses the SAME evDecks array (SU _scripts.js:374-387), so the population is identical in both variants; only the row controls differ.
- **Repository** — src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:74-83 — rows = decks filtered to `d.statusId === "assigned" || d.statusId === "jury_evaluation"` (plus the jury's own-assignment filter). Decks at `uploaded` / `pending_ai` / `manual_review` / `ai_evaluated` (src/pipeline/incubator.ts:15-19) can never appear. `grep -rn 'submit_for_ai' src/client` returns nothing, so the pipeline's own 'Submit for AI evaluation' transition (incubator.ts:33-38) has no UI on any screen.
- **Fix** — Widen the Evaluate row filter to the pre-assignment stages the prototype shows (uploaded / pending_ai / ai_evaluated, with the Evaluated badge for those already scored) while keeping the jury's own-assignment scoping, and expose the submit_for_ai / retry action from those rows.

### F0922 · `P1` · There is no evaluation due-date model, so every Due date / Submitted date / +/- Days / By Due date cell the jury screens specify has nothing behind it
*jassigned / alldecks / jurypipeline (all jury workflow screens) — data-columns · incubator · effort M · found on review*

- **Gap** — The auditor lists "Due date" as a missing COLUMN in claims 2, 5 and 6 without noticing that the underlying concept does not exist: there is nothing to render. Any fix to those three screens has to add an assignment deadline first (set at assign time, per deck × evaluator), then a submitted-at timestamp and the derived ± days, then hang the Remind action and the cron sweep off it.
- **Prototype** — panel-jassigned.html `<th>Due date</th>` fed by `d.due` in jaRender() (Jury _scripts.js:2804-2819); mpRender() (Jury _scripts.js:3089-3105) writes `<th>Due date</th>` in the default view and `<th>By Due date</th>` (rendered by `yn(d.onTime)`) in the submitted view, from `mpDecks[].due` / `.onTime`; Jury panel-jurypipeline.html carries `<th>Due date</th>`, `<th>Submitted date</th>` and `<th>+/- Days</th>` — the last being an explicit days-early/late delta against the deadline. _ADMIN-CONSOLE.html:838 also grants a **Remind** task per role, which only means something against a deadline.
- **Repository** — `grep -rni "due" src/ migrations/` returns only the VC "Due Diligence" nav section (src/shared/nav.ts:16,150-164) and QueryPage.tsx:39-54's OVERDUE_DAYS constant for founder queries. src/client/types.ts:69 gives DeckView only `assignedAt?` — no due date. No migration adds a due/deadline column to `decks` or to any assignment table. src/server/scheduled.ts:52-80 `runReminders` sweeps decks "parked at `assigned` with an assignee" — it fires on stage, not on a deadline, and there is no user-facing Remind action.
- **Fix** — Add `due_at` (and `submitted_at`) to the deck-assignment record in a migration, capture a due date in AssignPage's panel-4 confirm step, expose both on DeckView, derive `+/- days` in src/shared, then wire the three jury tables and re-point src/server/scheduled.ts at the deadline instead of the stage.
